title: GPU KV slab demarcation and live rewrite orchestrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a live, low-latency KV cache rewriter that reduces GPU memory fragmentation by introducing slab demarcation and a background rewrite orchestrator that cooperates with continuous batching and the serving runtime. The work targets long-running models with high KV churn where fragmentation causes OOM or unnecessary eviction churn during traffic peaks.
background: Our current KV allocation uses variable-sized slots and opportunistic compaction that can require stop-the-world or heavy tail latency when doing large compactions. Continuous batching increases throughput but can amplify hot-slot retention, leading to fragmentation islands on GPU memory. Existing tickets explore many allocator strategies, but customers are still hitting fragmentation-induced capacity cliffs on traffic spikes.
goals: 1) Reduce long-tail GPU memory fragmentation by 40% (measured by unusable free ranges) under representative workloads. 2) Avoid global pauses or blocking GC work that increases P95 latency by more than 5ms. 3) Integrate with continuous batching so rewrites are staged into normal request processing windows. 4) Provide operational knobs and telemetry to safely roll out behavior per-customer or per-model.
non_goals: We will not redesign the entire allocator heap shape or replace the kernel selection logic in this ticket. This is an incremental, deployable orchestrator that sits above the existing allocator and performs live rewrites; major allocator refactors will be tracked separately.
proposed_solution:
Introduce two coordinated pieces:

1) Slab demarcation metadata: augment each GPU memory slab with a compact fence structure (48 bytes) that records allocation epochs, hotness score, and a rewrite eligibility watermark. Slabs will be logically grouped into demarcation classes (small/medium/large-affinity) to avoid cross-size migration churn.

2) Live rewrite orchestrator: a background controller that schedules small, incremental rewrite transactions. A rewrite transaction copies live KV entries from fragmented regions into fresh slabs, updates indirection pointers, and atomically retires the old slots. The controller observes continuous batching windows and piggybacks small rewrite ops onto normal request batches when any request touches the slab being rewritten.

Key features:
- Probabilistic fencing: candidate slabs are sampled based on fragmentation heuristics and rewritten progressively to avoid hotspots.
- Rewrite windowing: rewrite work is budgeted in token/time slices per GPU to bound latency impact.
- Safe handover: the rewrite uses epoched indirection plus compare-and-swap updates so in-flight reads fall back to old slots until the swap completes.
- Eviction-aware policy: when eviction pressure is high, rewrite prioritization favors freeing contiguous ranges to recover contiguous capacity for large allocations.
data_structures: All fields are stored in existing allocator metadata pages with a new compact SlabFence struct. Indirection layer is a 64-bit pointer table (existing) accessed with epoch tags. No new large on-host side indexes; controller state is small and can be reconstructed from slab metadata on restart.
algorithms: 1) Fragmentation scoring: compute score = wasted_bytes / slab_size * hotness_decay. 2) Sampling: reservoir sample top-K candidate slabs per-GPU per-interval. 3) Incremental rewrite: for each candidate, copy N entries per transaction (N tuned by latency budget), update indirection table via CAS, mark old slot retired. 4) Reclamation: retired slots are coalesced lazily into free runs using an opportunistic hole-stitcher.
telemetry: Emit the following events and metrics: slab_fragmentation_score (gauge), eligible_rewrite_slabs (count), rewrite_transactions_started/completed (counters), rewrite_latency_histogram (ms), freed_contiguous_bytes (gauge), rewrite_backpressure_events (counter). Correlate with per-request P50/P95 latency and batch sizes. Surface a per-model fragmentation dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end system tests show fragmentation metric drops >= 40% on synthetic churn workload without increasing P95 request latency by more than 5ms. 2) No correctness regressions under concurrency tests (benchmarks with 100k concurrent KV touches). 3) Canary rollout (10% traffic) holds without increased OOMs or fatal errors for 48 hours. 4) Telemetry and debug endpoints available: /admin/rewrite_status and per-slab metadata dumps.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature flag off by default, internal staging rollout on dev cluster with synthetic churn jobs (2 weeks). Phase 2: Canary enable on a set of internal customers and non-critical models (10% traffic, 1 week). Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 50% with dynamic backoff enabled (2 weeks). Phase 4: Global enable with tune-up and ops runbook (monitoring alerts configured).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: CAS races could cause transient reads to observe inconsistent pointers. Mitigation: use double-checked epoch stamping and fallback reads that consult old slot until swap confirmed. Risk: rewrite work could starve compute for model inference. Mitigation: strict rewrite time budget and piggyback only when batching window slack exists. Risk: new metadata increases per-slab overhead. Mitigation: compact fence limited to 48 bytes and only allocated for active slabs.
testing_plan: Unit tests for SlabFence serialization and CAS semantics. Integration tests: multi-threaded correctness harness with random churn and compare to golden allocator. Load tests: replay real production traces with and without rewrites to measure P50/P95 and fragmentation. Fault injection: abrupt restarts during rewrite transactions to validate controller recovery.
notes: This ticket intentionally prioritizes minimal allocator surface changes to make the rollout lower risk. Follow-up work will evaluate richer coalescing heuristics and hardware-assisted memcpy optimizations. Assigning Marco to lead implementation and coordinate with infra for canary gating and observability dashboards. Schedule a design review with PM and SRE next Tuesday.
